correctness.rationale: The claim is reconstructed from the discrete last-zero factorization, an exact bridge occupation calculation, and two coefficient identities from \((1-z)^{-1/2}\). Conditioning on \(L_{2n}=2k\) leaves the pre-\(2k\) segment as a bridge because the no-later-zero event depends only on future increments. The terminal zero-free segment has symmetric sign. Exact exhaustive enumeration for \(1\le n\le9\) independently checks the distribution, conditional means, marginal means, coefficient identities, and covariance. No finite experiment is used to justify the all-\(n\) quantifier.

originality.rationale: The checked classical sources cover Brownian arcsine functionals, nonzero-boundary exit counts/last-exit times, and selected excursion-local joint laws, but the inspected statements do not give or imply the fixed-horizon conditional mean or covariance for last zero versus strict-positive occupation. value.rationale: Last zero and positive occupation are canonical path functionals tied to the arcsine phenomenon. The exact finite-horizon result shows a strictly negative dependence that disappears under Brownian scaling and quantifies that lattice correction at the natural \(n^{-1/2}\) rate. The conditional formula also identifies the mechanism: bridges with many zero visits depress strict-positive occupation. This is a motivated structural finite-sample fact rather than an arbitrary slice or table recomputation.
